critical_code_review_comments: Legal.jsx — DOMPurify config is correct: USE_PROFILES.html=true is the safe default; FORBID_TAGS explicitly removes script/iframe/object/embed/form/style; FORBID_ATTR removes the most common XSS attrs. useMemo on [content] is the right optimization. The sanitize call happens BEFORE dangerouslySetInnerHTML so React never sees raw untrusted HTML. NOTE: consider also adding `FORBID_ATTR: ['srcdoc','formaction','action']` for defense-in-depth, and explicitly setting `ALLOW_DATA_ATTR: false` to prevent data-* exfiltration vectors.

api.js — empty catch replaced with log.error including the malformed URL and the underlying error object. Good. Suggestion: also include `e?.message` truncated in production-safe form via the structured logger so prod builds (where log.error is a no-op) still surface this to Sentry / observability backend later.

AdminSettings.jsx — HIDDEN_PREFIXES=['danger_pin','_id'], HIDDEN_SUFFIXES=['_hash','_at'], HIDDEN_EXACT={'id','_id'} correctly filters sensitive keys. Suggestion: ALSO consider whitelisting via an explicit ALLOWED_KEYS array (registration_fee, payout_l1..l10, directs_required, vendor_commission_pct, auto_approve_on_payment, phone_reveal_fee, phone_reveal_gst_pct, shop_margin_enabled, service_booking_margin_enabled) — that way a future backend that introduces a new sensitive field like `webhook_secret` won't accidentally leak.
log.js — log.debug() level added; in production builds all 4 levels are silent so no PII leak risk. Good.
